thread.title: Will Video-Streaming Aggregator Roku Continue Its Rally?

author: TipRanks
title: Will Video-Streaming Aggregator Roku Continue Its Rally?
text:
Shares of Roku (NASDAQ: ROKU ), the California based over-the-top (OTT) television streaming platform, were on a rally mode last week. The rally was driven by bullish analyst sentiments, as Wall Street analysts see Roku gain a bigger share of the OTT television ecosystem. Here we use TipRanks data to take a closer look at what Wall Street's top analysts see in store for this volatile stock.
Roku provides devices that allow customers to access their favourite internet videos, similar to Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) TV, Google (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) (NASDAQ: GOOG ) Chromecast, or Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN ) Fire Stick. Moreover, the newly introduced Roku channel allows customers to stream hundreds of shows and movies it licenses directly from studios for free without a subscription, leaving tremendous scope for user base growth.
Investment bank Oppenhemier upgraded the stock’s rating from ‘perform’ to ‘outperform’ and also raised the price target to $50 (9% upside potential from the current share price). “The rapid adoption of The Roku Channel gives us incremental confidence in the channel's ability to garner viewership on other platforms, such as Samsung, allowing Roku to monetize a broader portion of the OTT ecosystem than we had previously assumed was possible,” Oppenheimer analyst Jason Helfstein said. Bear in mind that Helfstein is one of the Street’s best analysts. He is ranked 36 out of 4,836 analysts covered on TipRanks with a 69% success rate and an average return of 20.7% per rating.
The primary bullish factor is the expected increase in advertising revenue owing to the increasing popularity of the Roku channel. Helfstein expects Roku’s advertising business to massively add to its current user base of nearly 21 million, while also capturing a higher share of the $19 billion video advertising market. "We believe the Roku Channel is 0.63% of domestic time spent on Roku's platform or the 12th most-watched app by viewing hours, which represents a 9-million-hour monthly run-rate only nine months post-launch," Helfstein said.
From a fundamentals perspective, Roku posted an adjusted loss of 7 cents per share in the last quarter, way above market estimates of a loss of nearly 16 cents. Moreover, Roku’s quarterly revenues also surged 36% to $136.58 million. Moreover, the stock currently has a P/E ratio of 16.9 compared with 274 for Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX ). A Citron analytics report cites great upward potential for Roku, as they notice that having over 119 million paid subscribers and generating zero ad revenue, Netflix still has an enterprise value of $156 billion, while Roku has an enterprise value of about $3.5 billion, despite generating ad revenue and having nearly 17% of Netflix’s user base.
Following Roku’s IPO in November last year, the shares rallied to reach $50 a piece. Citron was then bearish on the streaming platform and stated that it feels the stock would go down to $28. However, the research firm is not against changing its perspective when the situation requires. "The move to cutting the cord and (over-the-top) advertising is real and it is a megatrend that Citron not only does not want to be short, but at this valuation I want to be long," Citron said in a note in May.
If we take a step back, we can see that the stock currently floats a cautiously optimistic Moderate Buy analyst consensus rating, with 3 analysts surveyed in the past 3 months having a buy rating on the stock and 3 having a neutral hold rating. It currently has a $42.83 price target with the high estimate reaching $50 and the low estimate being $30, indicating an 8.3% downside from current levels.
All in all, we believe it is dangerous to short these stocks or bet against them at the moment, given changing consumer preferences and the shift to digital platforms for television viewing.
